notes.title: The best PC games of 2013 - Saints Row IV
notes.notes:
I was singing within the first fifteen minutes of playing Saints Row IV. Riding an airborne nuclear missile, belting out Aerosmith's '98 classic "I Don't Want to Miss a Thing", my compatriots below bidding a final farewell to their fearless leader.

It probably sounded horrible. Not only because I'm completely tone deaf, but because I was also bellowing with laughter.

Volition's fourth and best open-world caper is a comedy masterpiece, managing to lampoon countless movies and games without missing a beat, and while it didn't exactly break any new ground with its mechanics or design, fun as they were, it's earned its spot as one of my Games of 2013 because it's so unrelentingly funny.

notes.title: Saints Row IV – PC Crossplay now enabled + Free Upgrade
notes.notes:
As we mentioned last week, crossplay is now live for Saints Row IV: Re-Elected across Steam, Epic and GOG Windows users! Your game should automatically upgrade to the Re-Elected version from whichever version you owned previously if you are on Windows, meaning if you didn’t already have all the DLC for the game – now you do!

Have fun in Steelport, Saints! 

[u][b]FAQ[/b][/u]
[b]Does this include Gat Out of Hell?
[/b]No, Saints Row Gat Out of Hell was a separate release, it was included in a double pack with SRIV: Re-Elected once but this is not the standard release. 

[b]I am in AUS – why can’t I play with my friend in another country? [/b]
Saints Row IV: Re-Elected has different content due to ratings in AUS, so you can only play with others on the same version as you. 

[b]Is there a way I can stop the upgrade and keep my version of Saints Row IV as it is? 
[/b]You can disable auto-update on GOG Galaxy if you have the game currently installed. (Cogwheel > Settings > Game features > Untick 'Auto-update games')
A Legacy Version of Saints Row IV will be also be available via a separate Beta Branch on GOG and Steam. 
To access the old version of Saints Row IV, right click on the game in your library, go to properties > beta and use the dropdown menu to select the version you want. 
for more help with this: https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/276C-85A0-C531-AFA3
However the differences between old and new versions will be minimal, and save games will be compatible.

[b]When will the Linux players get their upgrade? 
[/b]
We will update the community when we have a locked in date for this.

[b]Can Linux players crossplay now or do they have to wait? 
[/b]
Official support will come for Linux later – we will let you know when this is going to be available.

[b]Will Mods be affected? 
[/b]
Mods should not be affected, and should work as normal aside from any special cases where elements of the mod may clash with the code of the game.

notes.title: Sci-fi strategy game Stellaris joins Xbox Game Pass for PC this month

Microsoft has confirmed the latest batch of titles coming to Xbox Game Pass on PC - and while a few have been revealed previously, some new names, including sci-fi grand strategy game Stellaris, will also be making the leap to the subscription service before the month is through.

Alongside Stellaris, quirky (and tremendously entertaining) 60-second puzzle adventure Minit joins the Xbox Game Pass line-up on PC, as does F1 2018, a racer that Eurogamer's Martin Robison called "one of the very best F1 games to date" in his Recommended review last year.

notes.title: Dirt Rally 2.0, Cities: Skylines are the next additions to Xbox Game Pass on PC
notes.notes:
Microsoft has revealed the latest titles heading to its Xbox Game Pass subscription service for PC, and they look an awful lot like Dirt Rally 2.0, Saints Row 4, Cities: Skylines, and Bad North.

Cities: Skylines, of course, is developer Colossal Order's phenomenally popular city-builder, which, since its launch in 2015, has gone from strength to strength. Four years on, it's now received eight major expansions - After Dark, Snowfall, Natural Disasters, Mass Transit, Green Cities, Parklife, Industries, and Campus - plus an enormous number of free feature updates, and even a console release. Its enduring popularity is well-deserved too; it's a thoroughly entertaining urban planning and traffic management sim, and well worth checking out.

As for developer Volition's Saints Row 4: Re-Elected (which includes all DLC), it's a wonderfully idiotic spin on the open-world gangster genre, this time ramping up the ridiculousness to previously unseen heights. While early games in the series played it mostly straight, Saints Row 4 throws caution to the wind, delivering a game in which aliens trap our likeable rogue's gallery of heroes in a digital simulation of their beloved city of Steelport.

notes.title: de Blob owner THQ Nordic buys Saints Row and Dead Island owner Koch Media for 121m euro
notes.notes:
THQ Nordic, the company behind the Darksiders and de Blob re-releases, has bought Koch Media, owner of Saints Row and Dead Island publisher Deep Silver, in a deal worth 121m euro.

For that, THQ Nordic gets all of Deep Silver's studios and games, such as Volition (Saints Row), Dambuster (Homefront) and Dead Island. It also picks up Deep Silver's exclusive rights to the Metro games, which are developed by 4A.

In a note to press, THQ Nordic said it has no plans to restructure Deep Silver, which hopefully means jobs are safe (there are 150 people currently at Volition, for example), and Koch Media will continue to operate as a separate entity within the THQ Nordic group. It also said it plans to soldier on with Deep Silver's current slate of in-development games.

notes.title: The Joy of Saints Row s Johnny Gat
notes.notes:
A friend of mine started the Saints Row [official site] series with the fourth one. She loved having superpowers and trashing a virtual city, but she did wonder what the deal was with Johnny Gat. Even though he’s not in half the game spoilers for the third and fourth Saints Rows, but Johnny Gat dies and then comes back to life his absence is felt. Characters talk about how his loss changed them. The dude with the sunglasses and neck tattoos who seems like a generic video game badass is treated like he matters.

Gat’s a mascot for Saints Row, whether cameoing in games outside the series or within them. You start Saints Row: The Third with every member of the gang wearing an oversized Gat mask during a bank robbery even Gat himself has one, pointless as that makes the disguise. Everybody wants to be Johnny Gat. To understand why he has that reputation, why fans love him while outsiders roll their eyes, we have to go back to Saints Row 2.

notes.title: Steam Workshop for Saints Row IV is live!
notes.notes:
The Saints Row series is all about the freedom to play how you want, and we're now taking that one step further with Steam Workshop support for Saints Row IV PC! It's never been easier to create and install mods that add new weapons and clothing, run custom scripts, and change gameplay values. Head over to the Saints Row IV community hub in your Steam client, click the Workshop tab, and start browsing. It's just that easy! 
  
To celebrate, Saints Row IV PC is on sale for 75% off on Steam all this week and next! 
http://store.steampowered.com/app/206420/ 

There were many challenges in implementing Steam Workshop support since the game was not originally designed to support modding. A handful of dedicated Volition devs worked on this in their free time to update the engine and remove memory restrictions, as well as finding a way for individual mods to interact and work correctly with each other without the need for running special tools. It was all a labor of love for our fans, and we're incredibly excited to see the crazy content you come up with! 
  
One last extra special thanks to the modding community at http://saintsrowmods.com who worked with us on creating and improving the tools, along with all the testing and feedback over the last few years. We couldn't have done it without you! 
  
[i]* Please note that only the Windows version of Saints Row IV PC is currently compatible with Workshop. We hope to announce Linux support soon. [/i]

notes.title: Wot I Did On My Staycation
notes.notes:
As you didn’t notice, I’ve been away for the last three months, to focus on helping raise the child which will one day destroy the universe. In between prising the crushed, partially-chewed remains of smaller star systems from her tiny, iron grip, I managed to play a few videogames. Some for a while, but most only for a couple of hours. Despite myself, it was difficult not to have opinions about them, and to want to write those opinions on some manner of ‘web’ ‘site.’ I bided my time. I waited. And now here I am, able to force you to listen to my single-sentence opinions on 13 recent videogames – the likes of Saints Row IV, Gone Home, The Bureau, Papers Please and even that car-stealing thing on console. For the first time on RPS, I have even included a rating for each game.

notes.title: Saints Row IV: Enter The Dominatrix Dropping This Month
notes.notes:
Once upon a time, Saints Row IV didn’t even have its own number – let alone a snazzy, posh purple Roman numeral. It was nascent, in a pre-life phase that many organisms have known at some point or another. That is to say, an expansion to Saints Row: The Third. Back then, it was known as Enter The Dominatrix – at least, until THQ (may it sue still-existent companies from beyond the grave in peace) set it on its course to sequeldom. But now Saints Row IV is getting a DLC expansion titled “Enter The Dominatrix,” and it’s, er, a different sort of thing. More literal, I would say. There is an actual dominatrix. From the looks of things, you will be, um, entering someone in a fashion. Yeah.

(more…)

notes.title: Headcase: Saint’s Row IV First-Person Mod
notes.notes:
There isn’t much that Volition didn’t cram into Saint’s Row IV. The design is a tombola of ridiculous things, a churning barrel of awesome nonsense that you randomly pluck fun from, and then give a child a teddy bear. Hmm, I over-analogised that one. Not that you shouldn’t give a child a teddy bear, but if you do it after every moment of fun in this open-world nonsense generator you’d better have lots of bears and lots of children. And I’m about to make that unlikely scenario even more problematic with the Saints Row IV First Person View mod. It makes it even more fun.

notes.title: DEVOLVER DIGITAL AND DEEP SILVER BRING MORE WANG TO SHADOW WARRIOR
notes.notes:
Developers Flying Wild Hog and Volition, along with the publisher illuminati of Devolver Digital and Deep Silver, are excited to announce an unprecedented cross promotion between Shadow Warrior and Saints Row IV. Through this groundbreaking show of absurdity, owners of Saints Row IV on Steam will unlock the legendary ‘Penetrator’ weapon in Flying Wild Hog’s reimagined Shadow Warrior as a powerful-but-elegant alternative to the traditional katana. Yep, read that again.

“I’m sorry I can’t really hear you over the sound of all that money being thrown at screens around the world,” said Fork Parker, Devolver Digital CFO. “And I don’t know what to tell you other than you can now wield a giant purple dildo from Saints Row IV in Shadow Warrior. There’s your headline, nerds.”

Again, not sure what else to tell you all that hasn’t been summed up already. If you own Saints Row IV on Steam and purchase Shadow Warrior, you can literally use the big purple Penetrator in place of a katana in Shadow Warrior to sever the heads off of demons. We know, and yet we can’t really believe it ourselves.

Shadow Warrior is set to launch via Steam for PC on September 26, 2013. Saints Row IV is currently available for Steam, Xbox 360, and PlayStation 3.

For updated information on development, follow @_ShadowWarrior on Twitter or visit [url=www.shadowwarrior.com]www.shadowwarrior.com[/url].

Normally I wouldn’t even bat an eyelash at some random cross-game promotional effort – let alone dedicate precious RPS Hyper Maturity Space to it – but this time is different. The reason? Two of the dumbest, most laughably enjoyable games I’ve played in ages are colliding, and there is now no way that last clause wasn’t a euphemism for something, authorial intent be damned. Yes, it’s finally happening: Saints Row The Third‘s infamous dildo bat is invading another game. I know, I know. notes.title: Announcing the New Deep Silver Volition Super-Powered Community Support Team!
notes.notes:
We understand that the most important resource we have is our fans. While Jeffrey Strike (Deadly Cyclone) has done a fantastic job in helping us out with moderating the forums on his personal time, we realize that there is still a pressing need for broader technical support and even more communication with our community. In order to provide our players with the best possible experience, we have formed a new super powered support team. Our primary goal is to interact with the community in order to identify and fix any ongoing issues, as well as provide the very best support to our customers. We will also make an effort to communicate what's going on behind the scenes with the status of bug fixes and patches, and keep the community up to date.

So, let's meet the team!

Mike Watson ([V] IdolNinja) – Community Manager – Mike has a long history of modding the Saints Row games and brings with him a deep understanding of how our games work. He also has over 10 years of experience in IT support management, and is a long-time moderator of the saintsrowmods.com forum which currently boasts over 67,000 members.

Maurice Tan (Professor Pew) – Deep Silver International Community Manager – Maurice works on every title Deep Silver publishes, which is why he hasn't been around enough on the forums lately! (Sorry! -- Maurice) He makes sure that whenever fans ask for something on forums or social media, someone at Deep Silver will hear about it over and over again.

Ben Brenner – Saints Row IV QA Lead – Ben has worked on the Saints Row franchise since Saints Row 2. His forum experience includes forum moderator for several Shareplay games from 1996 to 2002.  He also helped moderate forums on Red Faction Armageddon.

Brendon Ellis (VEllix) – Technical Audio Support – Brendon is an audio bugfixer on Saints Row IV, and was an audio tester on Saints Row: The Third and Red Faction Armageddon, and a gameplay tester on Saints Row 2 and Red Faction Guerrilla. He’s lurked the Saintsrow.com forums since Saints Row: The Third’s release, occasionally posting when he felt helpful, but now he’ll be taking a more focused initiative to assist.

Christina Kniskern (Cirose) – QA Tester – Christina has been at Volition since 2008 and has worked on Saints Row 2, Red Faction: Armageddon, Saints Row: The Third, Saints Row IV and DLC. Her focus has been on Audio and Gameplay testing but she also has experience in most other areas. She’s been around the forums but not in an official capacity until now.

Derek Wade (VUncleSam) – PC QA Tester – Derek has been working on Saints Row 4 since early March. He has several years of experience moderating forums for various communities in competitive semi-pro and casual settings for games such as Crysis 2, Battlefield: Bad Company 2, Call of Duty 2 and more. (Lots of 2’s!)

Ryan Mansfield (VRyan) – QA Tester – Ryan has worked on games for both the Saints Row and Red Faction franchises. He has also spent several years assisting in moderating forums and Twitch channels for MLG. With time on each platform, he has spent the majority of his time on Saints Row IV as part of the UI team.

You may notice certain support threads and subforums being moved or expanded while we attempt to sort everything out. We have a lot of work ahead of us, but we are all deeply committed to making sure that everyone can enjoy our games. You deserve nothing less.

Thank you!

Clint Ourso (V_Geaux93)
Studio Production Manager
Deep Silver Volition
